etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin dēvōtus, past participle of Latin dēvoveō (“dedicate by a vow, sacrifice oneself, promise solemnly”). Doublet of devow; see also devout. Displaced native Middle English ēstful, from Old English ēstful.

definitions.definition: to give one's time, focus one's efforts, commit oneself, etc. entirely for, on, or to a certain matter

quote.citation: 1678, Obadiah Grew, Meditations Upon Our Saviour's Parable of The Prodigal Son:
quote.text: He is the Chief of this far Countrey; and to his service, carnal and wicked men devote themselves.
a leafless and simple branch  […]  devoted to the purpose of climbing
